BUILT, CONFIRMED FAILING, then FIXED, all this session. First pass found large conditional divergence masked by good marginals (duration/SIRET presence are schema/era step-functions in real data, flat in synthetic; CPV missingness strongly schema+notice_type-conditional in real data, nearly uniform in synthetic). Fixed via schema-conditional duration, year-regime-conditional SIRET, and schema x notice_type-conditional CPV rates (empirically swept against real per-cell targets), plus a root-cause fix to notices.py's schema_family assignment (hard Oct-2023 cutoff -> probabilistic draw using real by-year EFORMS-adoption shares, which also fixed schema_family_mix as a side effect). Post-fix: CPV missing by schema/notice_type now within 1-3pp of real; SIRET by year-regime within a few points, most years <6pp; duration matches almost exactly for LEGACY years and 2024, undershoots by 10-12pp for 2025/2026 (documented residual -- would need a 3rd, year-varying LEGACY parameter to close). Residual open items: pre-2024 CPV year-trend not modeled, and the by-year notice-VOLUME density-ramp problem (separate from schema assignment, still open, see marginal_fidelity's schema_family_mix history).

Identifier-missing vs CPV-missing phi correlation is positive (0.051 after adding schema/year-conditional corruption; was 0.121 originally, dropping through 0.113/0.088/0.109 across intermediate recalibrations) in the synthetic pilot -- evidences the dependent-corruption mechanism is still working directionally, but the correlation weakened once duration/SIRET/CPV missingness gained independent schema/year-driven variation on top of the shared quality-class driver (two partially-uncorrelated sources of missingness dilute their combined co-occurrence signal) -- was not compared against the real corpus's calib_missingness_phi_matrix.csv value at v0.1; magnitude match unverified either way.
Gini recalibrated from 0.641 to 0.814 (target 0.832, tolerance +/-0.15) during this build; within tolerance.
